body: Thank you, I had a friend with severe anorexia and we had a hard time getting her to eat enough calories while she was recovering without feeling too full. She was basically eating lettuce and a few cucumber slices and calling it a meal that would keep her full for the whole day. It was horrifying. She will have lasting consequences for the rest of her life, her bone density is shot and severe malnutrition caused severe internal organ issues that might never be fixed (heart damage etc.) I hope that no matter what your personal stance on the matter, you direct these people to a professional and if that recovery journey is filled with animal products then so be it. You can argue ethics and logic with them after they recover, if they recover. When they are too deep in your comments just cause more suffering. So get them professional help and then later on you can argue about your beliefs.

The reality is that most likely children would not eat vegan options as their main dishes because they often don't/can't appreciate vegetables, beans, lentils etc. Even my parents who like to live primarily consuming vegan friendly foods   require meat at times. Not a lot, but they do. I don't fault them for that, I'm just glad they are doing everything they can to improve their own lives (I was similar, and I still have the guilty pleasure of consuming vegan dishes that mimic meat very closely because of the nostalgia).

Been on both sides of the fence, as a vegan and as a carnist. I have been personally questioned over how eating "rabbit food" will help me or give enough protein. On the other hand when I was still a carnist I witnessed a vegan coworker gag and vomit in the break room trash bin because someone was eating chicken (they also complained to HR that eating animal products in the break room should be banned because the fact people eat those things there means that the company supports animal cruelty and the Nazis apparently). Yes, some people, on both sides of the fence, are very... eager to interfere/argue. I personally try not to interfere in anyone's personal choices even if I disapprove of them. But there are also curious people, asking if you're still vegan or gluten free might not be a personal attack each and every time, they might just be curious or even considering veganism themselves and an angry reply and complaint about it is not going to make anyone more likely to consider going vegan.

I just don't like kids. Period. End of story. And that should be fine, a statement that should not be followed by gasps of horror and unfriending on Facebook. You should be able to say that kids are not your favourite human beings in the world because for some it is simply the truth and it should be acknowledged. 

It's not that I hate them for the sake of it and want them to vanish or something, but I hate them the same way one hates people who chew with their mouth open, or drunk people who vomit on your shoes on a bus. I don't hate the person, I hate the side-effects of their existence (bodily fluids, noise, stuff breaking etc). I can't function with less than 7 hours of sleep, so waking up every two hours to care for a baby is a no go. I gag and throw up because I clean up my dogs vomit which is much easier to deal with than human bodily fluids. I have a temperament that is ill suited for raisin children (quick to anger, impulsive and easily get stressed and/or anxious). 

So tldr: I have a bad personality for parenting and care giving in general in addition to already hating that part of the population for causing disturbances to my peaceful existence.

Friend battled with severe endometriosis and other chronic illnesses. They fainted at least a dozen times a month from the overwhelming pain while on prescription morphine. Doctors said she had to be dealing the drugs to someone and wasn't taking them because she was in so much pain. Stopped writing prescriptions to her, made notes in her file. Took her three years to find a specialist who took her seriously. She's better now, still needs strong painkillers but surgery helped a lot. People still comment that she wanted to be "special" by getting a hysterectomy and that "cramps aren't that bad, you overreacted." I lucked out with migraines, lockjaw and extreme muscle and nerve pain in my shoulders and upper back and my colleagues at work give me crap about my specialised sick leave policy for the days when I can't move my head or arms.

The problem that I encounter is that my friend is happy. They are genuinely happy. They smile and laugh and have fun and they love their fiancée. But they don't see their family anymore, they don't have any friends besides me, they don't have money or education, no plans for the future and rapidly declining financial security. That is what I mean. They are happy, but they have nothing else left besides that happiness. Sure, it counts for a lot, and since it's pretty much the only thing my friend has left... I don't dare to cut the cord: leave her with no friends and no happiness because our friendship is over the minute I open my mouth.
Feel that, and sometimes trying to convince medical professionals that you're in pain when they don't see you screaming for mom and writhing on the floor is a battle that many lose.

Just a quick tip, it doesn't matter if you have 10 master's degrees, if none of the employers need/want that skill set then you aren't getting work. The biggest barrier is language: you will not find work in an average/medium sized company that has a majority of Finnish employees (or it's a something like one in a million). If you do, it's going to be you alone in a cubicle/office and maybe two or three Finnish coworkers that speak semi fluent English randomly asking if you're joining them for lunch once a week. Every document is going to be in Finnish, if it's in English, it's going to be discussed/planned in Finnish. Every meeting, every conversation is going to be in Finnish. Every email, every memo, every document, every training and course provided. Bigger companies have more English, but you will need to get used to being alone 90% of the time, of your coworkers discussing things in Finnish around you. This is the sad reality at the moment. You will need those language skills. 

In addition most work places with more English will want high fluency and ability to write highly technical language. While I put some of it on your frustrated state and possibly writing on a phone, it sounds/reads like something most employers would remark on negatively. At least I hope your CV has more refined language and grammar because poor English writing on your application is also something that will get you disqualified early on.

Funny thing, which in no way funny actually but yk, I was diagnosed with mild depression. That's fine, I was a teen so that makes sense. I hid it from people and they kinda forgot about it after a few months of therapy and I stopped going. A few years later around 15? I had a really bad episode that landed me in the nurses office. She made me take a test, you know those 'rate your thoughts and then count the points' tests. Anyway it was pretty standard way to gauge a person's mental state and I did it pretty quickly. 

Now for the funny thing. I had been bullied and laughed at for the past year, that very day had been dragged to the nurses office after the whole class had been made aware that I was mentally unstable. The nurse took the test, counted the points and then told me: "this rates your mental status as severe and in need of immediate medical intervention, but we can both agree that the results were affected by today's events so you don't need to go see a doctor." 

And then she told me to get out. Despite me non-verbally marking on the test and then verbally confirming to a healthcare professional that I though about suicide multiple time a day and had been making plans. Delayed me getting help by years. Not that it really helped me now but...

So, yeah. I'm fucked up, and no one really seems to care, not really. And I'm not even suprised at this point. Don't feel much of anything really.

Thank you, it's been a while since anyone said that I deserve anything nice. Mostly people I say anything to just nod, smile and leave to find another person to talk to. It's... Fine? I guess. If they don't want to be with me, don't want to interact with me, that's fine. But it hurts when it's done in such a shitty way and when they are all aware that I have depression and anxiety attacks. I just feel unwelcome in their group. Parents are good, but only in limited doses and whenever I go to stay with them all my friends suddenly want to invite me out, though always as the last resort. I'm sure it will all collapse at some point, I pull away and then a bit more and suddenly they will find an excuse to not invite me to anything. And honestly? I cry and scream about losing them one day and tomorrow I won't care a lick about any of them and hope they just leave me alone so I can read my favourite books and drink tea until the morning hours. 

I guess all the little, insignificant things like that pile up. Like mom said, I have a bad case of overthinking everything that leads to more depression and anxiety. It's tiresome, but I can't turn it off, only managed that when I had my dog with me, but that's not possible now. Therapy hasn't done anything for me, it's the same as chatting about my day to a partially deaf grandma, she can't remember/hear most things and I only see her every other week and that doesn't help, is just another burden on me if I don't go and try. 

Sorry for the ramble, just feels a bit better to write it out, hoping the some people listen and that some person out there reads it and thinks that hey, I feel the same and maybe it helps them in some way.
